Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: production 2D isometric strategy-game death sprite sheet. Reference image is only for exact character identity, palette, pixel-art/rendered style and camera. Generate a NEW six-frame death animation of that same character on a genuinely transparent background. Arrange EXACTLY 3 equal columns and 2 equal rows, six separate non-overlapping frames, reading left to right top row then bottom row. Every cell same scale, same camera (slightly elevated isometric, facing screen-right), fixed ground baseline 85% down each cell, same center ground anchor. Generous padding, all equipment entirely inside its cell. No labels, no grid lines, no floor, no text, no blood, no detached body parts, no background or shadow baked in. Preserve convincing three-dimensional volume, foreshortening, overlapping limbs and armor highlights. A body must articulate and buckle, NEVER rotate a rigid standing sprite. Final frame is the permanent settled corpse, lying naturally on its side in isometric ground perspective with clear contact and rounded volume. Character must stay exactly the same physical size throughout the six frames; do not enlarge the lying body.
Same steel-helmeted swordsman, cream tabard with crimson shoulders, red kite shield, sword and boots. Frame 1 upright reacting to hit; frame 2 knees bending and torso pitching; frame 3 one knee on ground, shield tilted supporting weight; frame 4 torso turning onto hip and shoulder, legs folding; frame 5 body contacting ground on side with bent knees, shield leaning by arm; frame 6 settled on side with head, shoulders and hips at believable depths, sword resting beside hand, shield partly overlaps torso. Head ends toward screen-right. The last frames must look like a solid armored human resting on the ground, not a flattened sticker.

Frame 1 mounted horse stumbling facing right; frame 2 forelegs buckle, horse chest drops, rider pitches forward; frame 3 knees touch ground while hindquarters follow, rider loses seat; frame 4 horse rolls onto side, rider tumbles alongside (do not fuse their bodies); frame 5 heavy horse flank contacts ground, legs fold, rider rests beside saddle; frame 6 fully settled horse lying on side, rounded barrel clearly volumetric, tucked legs, horse head toward right, knight and dropped lance beside it, no duplicate rider. Horse maintains mass and anatomy, rider motion lags horse. Non-graphic.
